interpretation.diagram_classification: theological diagram (Trinitarian diagram, of the 'Scutum fidei' / Shield of the Trinity type, in an inverted triangular form with a central crucifix)
interpretation.interpretation: The diagram sets out the relations between the three persons of the Trinity and the one God. The three outer circles carry the labels PATER, a hard-to-read word in the upper right circle (probably 'spiritus sanctus') and FILIVS. They are joined to one another by the outer sides of the triangle, which bear the text "non est", meaning that one person is not the other. Each outer circle is joined to the central circle DEVS by a band bearing "est", meaning that each person is God. The central circle therefore expresses the unity of the divine essence, and the outer circles express the distinction of persons. The crucifix on the vertical axis between DEVS and FILIVS may refer to the incarnation and passion of the Son, and it strengthens the link between the central divinity and the Son. The diagram is a visual summary of Trinitarian doctrine: three persons who are distinct from one another and each fully God.
interpretation.evidence: The labels PATER, FILIVS and DEVS and the repeated formulae "non est" (on the outer sides) and "est" (on the bands to the centre) form the known logic of the Trinitarian shield diagram. The upper right label is not clearly legible in Step 1, where I marked it as illegible, so reading it as the Holy Spirit relies on the symmetry of the scheme and not on the transcription. In Step 1, entry 4 calls the central band connection 'to the head of the cross' with the text "est", and the connection of DEVS to the crucified figure is of medium certainty. The crucifix is not part of the standard shield schema, so its meaning as a reference to the Son's incarnation and sacrifice is an interpretation from visual and iconographic knowledge. Step 1 entries 1 and 5-6 give the "non est" bands as links between PATER and the upper right circle, and between each of these and FILIVS. This is consistent with the scheme.
